intended_object: A pointwise representative (via the `Lp` coercion to a function) of the L² Hilbert transform of the "good part" from the library's Calderón–Zygmund stopping-time decomposition of an integrable f. This comes from the docstring and from its use in the weak-(1,1) proof for the maximal Hilbert transform.
explanation: The body just applies the `Lp` coercion `⇑` to `ordinaryHilbertTransformL2 (stoppingGoodPartL2 f hf)`. It picks a function on ℝ out of an L² equivalence class. That class depends on a stopping-time good/bad split built inside the library's own proof. The definition exists so that later lemmas can state a.e. strong measurability and L² norm facts about this one function, and so that the function can be swapped for a measurable version (lines 2404–2416) inside the weak-(1,1) argument. It is a helper object for the proof, not a standard mathematical notion: the good part of this particular decomposition, viewed through one chosen representative. So it cannot be judged as faithful or not against an object in the literature.
